metadata.title: An Ogilvy Lens on SectorBrief — Gayatri
metadata.ogilvy_note: Food for thought — not a grade. Ogilvy is one lens among several, running alongside the course rubric. The maker decides.

beats.narration_text: Gayatri's SectorBrief pitch. Sector-by-sector market intelligence, automated — AI reads and ranks industry news, delivers one clean report to your inbox in under a minute. It is already live. What would David Ogilvy ask about it?

props.command: I just watched Gayatri's SectorBrief pitch — sector-by-sector market intelligence, automated. AI reads and ranks industry news, delivers one clean report to your inbox in ~45 seconds. The product is already live. What do David Ogilvy's principles say about how this pitch frames the work? Not a score. Just the questions a great ad man would ask.

beats.role_note: Show Slide 1, rebuild. The tagline is strong Ogilvy copy — earns its place.
beats.narration_text: Let's start with the tagline on Slide 1. Your industry's news, read and ranked by AI — delivered to your inbox in under a minute. That is close to Ogilvy copy. It is specific, it names the mechanism, it gives a time. The live product URL is there too, at the bottom. Ogilvy would ask: why is the product buried at the footer of the title slide instead of being the headline?

beats.act: LENS 1 — The Human Cost: What Does the Analyst Miss?
beats.role_note: Show Slide 2 (problem), rebuild. 10-15 hrs/week is strong — but what's the human cost?
beats.narration_text: Slide 2 — the problem. Two to three hours lost daily. Ten to fifteen hours a week scanning instead of acting. Those numbers are strong. Fragmented sources, no prioritization, doesn't scale. Ogilvy: always find the human cost behind the time cost. Ten to fifteen hours is the input. What does that analyst miss while scanning? What deal goes unflagged? What competitor move lands late? That is the slide this number is reaching for.

beats.act: LENS 2 — The Buried Lead: It Is Live Right Now
beats.role_note: Show Slide 9 (live POC), rebuild. The live product is the most powerful fact — it is on Slide 9.
beats.narration_text: Slide 9 — proof of concept. And here is the line: this isn't a mockup. It's live right now. Anyone watching this video could open this link and use it today. Ogilvy said the most powerful word in advertising is 'free.' But running close behind it is 'now.' This product is live. That is the headline. It is sitting on Slide 9. The question worth sitting with: what if it opened the pitch?

beats.act: LENS 3 — The Competition Slide: Others Force a Trade-off
beats.role_note: Show Slide 7 (competition), rebuild. The headline is close to Ogilvy-perfect.
beats.narration_text: Slide 7 — competition. Others force a trade-off. SectorBrief doesn't. Multi-sector coverage, AI prioritization, zero setup — competitors give you at most two of three. That is a tight, precise claim. Google Alerts does not analyze. Feedly does not rank. Hiring an analyst caps at two sectors and costs a salary. Ogilvy: specifics in a comparison always outperform generalities. This table earns its place. The headline is the whole pitch in nine words.

beats.act: LENS 4 — The Free Tier Is the Ask
beats.role_note: No slide needed. The $0 tier makes 'use it now' the strongest possible CTA.
beats.narration_text: There is a free tier. One sector, daily report, zero setup required. Ogilvy was explicit: a free offer is your most powerful acquisition tool. The ask slide requests feedback on conversion and customer introductions. Those are useful. But the product is live, it has a free tier, and the audience is watching right now. The most direct ask in this pitch is the one not stated: go use it today. Why is that not the last line?

beats.act: LENS 5 — The Close: From Live to Paying
beats.role_note: Show Slide 10 (ask), rebuild. The ask is from live to paying — sharpen it.
beats.narration_text: Slide 10 — the ask. Help us take SectorBrief from live product to paying customers. Two asks: feedback on conversion, and introductions to analysts and CI teams. The goal is ten pilot customers in sixty days. That is specific and right-sized. Ogilvy: a close should be specific enough to act on. This one is. The question worth sitting with: the product already works. What does a free trial day actually look like for one of those ten pilots?

beats.role_note: Not a verdict: four questions for the next draft.
beats.narration_text: Not a verdict — a lens set. Four questions for the next draft. One: the product is live today — why is that on Slide 9? Two: what does an analyst miss while scanning for three hours? Three: others force a trade-off — that headline is the whole pitch, does it lead? Four: you have a free tier, why not end with 'use it now'? These are Ogilvy's questions. The pitch decides which ones matter.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take your deck into Claude and try this: here are four Ogilvy questions about my pitch. For each one — which specific slide is most in play, and what is one alternative frame to consider? Not a correction, just another angle. The goal is not to score the pitch. Ogilvy is one lens. The course rubric is another.
